title: How people opt in to texts from Yuppers.app
description: Each step a person takes to receive text messages from Yuppers.app, with the exact wording of every screen and message.
intro: Yuppers.app (https://yuppers.app) sends text messages in two programs, Yuppers.app sign-in codes and Yuppers.app agreement updates, and for nothing else: no marketing. This page shows each step a person takes to receive them, with a picture of each screen and the exact wording it shows.
note: On yuppers.app and in the Yuppers mobile app, signing in with a phone number and the “Text updates” control on an agreement appear only while texting is turned on for the service. The screens below show them as they appear when texting is enabled.
websiteIntro: These screens were captured from the Yuppers website, https://yuppers.app, on a phone-sized screen.
mobileIntro: The Yuppers app for iPhone and Android has the same steps: signing in with a phone number, and the “Text updates” control on an agreement. Each picture is the whole screen, under the app’s own navigation bar.
mobileRelease: The Yuppers app is not yet published in the App Store or Google Play, so these pictures were taken from the app’s own screens, built from its code and shown at the size of an iPhone screen, rather than from a store download.
mobileSame: The same consent texts and confirmation are used on the website and in the app, and so are the texts that follow: the confirmation text in {confirmationText} and the HELP and STOP replies in {replies}.
programs: Yuppers.app sign-in codes: one text for each code a person asks for, to sign in, to confirm deleting their account, or to add a number to their account, and only once they have ticked a box beside the number.
Yuppers.app agreement updates: one text per status change of an agreement the person turned updates on for. Message frequency varies; there is no fixed maximum.

signIn.title: Step 1. Entering a phone number to sign in
signIn.caption: The sign-in form takes an email address or a phone number. As soon as what is typed reads as a phone number, an unticked box appears beside the consent text below, whose two addresses are links to the terms and the privacy policy. “Send code” stays disabled until the box is ticked, and the form says why. Under the button are links to the section on text messages in the privacy policy, to the privacy policy and to the terms.
signIn.alt: The Yuppers sign-in form on a phone, with a phone number entered, an unticked box beside the consent text with links to the terms and the privacy policy, the Send code button disabled, and the line saying to tick the box first.

boxTicked.title: Step 2. Ticking the box
boxTicked.caption: Once the person ticks the box, “Send code” is enabled. Pressing it asks for one text with a sign-in code; nothing is sent before.
boxTicked.alt: The same sign-in form with the box beside the consent text ticked and the Send code button enabled.

codeSent.title: Step 3. After asking for a code
codeSent.caption: The screen says where the code went and asks for it. The text that carries the code is shown below the picture.
codeSent.alt: The Yuppers sign-in form after a code was sent: the number it went to, and a field for the six-digit code.

textUpdates.title: Step 4. Turning on text updates for an agreement
textUpdates.caption: On an agreement the person is a party to, “Text updates” shows an unticked box beside the consent wording below, whose two addresses are links to the terms and the privacy policy. Nothing is sent unless the person ticks the box and presses Save. If the account has no phone number yet, the person first enters a US number, which we check with a one-time code sent to it only once they tick a box beside the last quoted text below. The text that carries that code is shown after it.
textUpdates.alt: The Text updates section of an agreement on a phone: an unticked box beside the consent wording, with links to the terms and the privacy policy, and a Save button.

confirmation.title: Step 5. After ticking the box and saving
confirmation.caption: The screen confirms that text updates are on for this agreement, says how often and to which number they go, and how to stop them.
confirmation.alt: The Text updates section after saving: the box ticked, and the confirmation that text updates are on, with the number partly hidden.

confirmationText.title: Step 6. The opt-in confirmation text
confirmationText.caption: Sent at once to the number, as received:

replies.title: Step 7. HELP and STOP
replies.caption: Replying HELP or STOP to any of our texts is answered at once with these texts. STOP ends every text from Yuppers.app to that number, sign-in codes included, until it replies START; the person can still sign in with an email address. Each status update afterwards looks like the last text below.

signIn.title: Step 1. Entering a phone number to sign in, in the app
signIn.caption: The app’s sign-in screen takes an email address or a phone number. As soon as what is typed reads as a phone number, an unticked box appears beside the same consent text as on the website, whose two addresses are links that open in the browser. “Send code” stays disabled until the box is ticked, and the screen says why. Under the button are links to the section on text messages in the privacy policy, to the privacy policy and to the terms, which open in the browser.
signIn.alt: The sign-in screen of the Yuppers app, phone-sized, with a phone number entered, an unticked box beside the consent text with links to the terms and the privacy policy, the Send code button disabled, and the line saying to tick the box first.

boxTicked.title: Step 2. Ticking the box, in the app
boxTicked.caption: In the app too, once the person ticks the box, “Send code” is enabled. Pressing it asks for one text with a sign-in code, the same text as on the website; nothing is sent before.
boxTicked.alt: The sign-in screen of the Yuppers app with the box beside the consent text ticked and the Send code button enabled.

codeSent.title: Step 3. After asking for a code, in the app
codeSent.caption: The app says where the code went and asks for it. The code comes in the same text as on the website.
codeSent.alt: The sign-in screen of the Yuppers app after a code was sent: the number it went to, and a field for the six-digit code.

textUpdates.title: Step 4. Turning on text updates for an agreement, in the app
textUpdates.caption: On an agreement the person is a party to, the app’s “Text updates” section shows an unticked box beside the consent wording below, whose two addresses are links to the terms and the privacy policy. Nothing is sent unless the person ticks the box and presses Save. “How we text you” opens this page. If the account has no phone number yet, the person first enters a US number, which we check with a one-time code sent to it only once they tick a box beside the last text below.
textUpdates.alt: The Text updates section of an agreement in the Yuppers app: an unticked box beside the consent wording, with links to the terms and the privacy policy, and a Save button.

confirmation.title: Step 5. After ticking the box and saving, in the app
confirmation.caption: The app confirms that text updates are on for this agreement, says how often and to which number they go, and how to stop them.
confirmation.alt: The Text updates section in the Yuppers app after saving: the box ticked, and the confirmation that text updates are on, with the number partly hidden.

verifyCodeText: The text with the code that checks a number being added:
moreHeading: The terms and the privacy policy
more: Both programs are described in the section on text messages of the {terms} and of the {privacy}.

replies.help: Yuppers.app: Text updates about your agreements and sign-in codes. Help: support@yuppers.app or https://yuppers.app/help. Msg & data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out.
replies.stop: Yuppers.app: You're unsubscribed and will get no more texts from us. You can still sign in with your email address. Reply START to resubscribe.
